name: Modern internal service baseline
description: For internet-facing or high-value internal services. TLS 1.2 minimum, no CBC/static-RSA suites, forward secrecy, server cipher preference, secure renegotiation, OCSP stapling and HSTS required.

checks.message: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated (RFC 8996) and must be disabled.
Supporting TLS 1.3 removes the need for much of the legacy suite surface.
RC4, export, NULL and anonymous suites must never be accepted.
CBC suites with SHA-1 MACs and static-RSA key exchange are weak; prefer AEAD with ECDHE.
Without forward secrecy, a stolen private key decrypts recorded traffic.
A server that follows client suite order lets a client steer it to the weakest suite it accepts.
RFC 5746 secure renegotiation prevents the 2009 prefix-injection attack.
Client-initiated renegotiation is an unauthenticated CPU/DoS amplifier.
Stapling keeps revocation checking private and fast for clients.
Without HSTS, the first request over plain HTTP can be intercepted.
A short max-age leaves a window for repeated downgrade attempts.
includeSubDomains protects sibling hostnames that may be weaker.
An expired or near-expiry certificate causes outages and trains users to click through warnings.
Keys below 2048-bit RSA / 256-bit EC are not acceptable in 2026.
SHA-1 and MD5 certificate signatures are forgeable and rejected by modern clients.
